Single Responsibility: each class/module has one responsibility; each file is one cohesive unit. Open/Closed: extend without modifying existing code. Liskov: subclasses remain substitutable. Interface Segregation: clients depend only on used interfaces. Dependency Inversion: high-level modules depend on abstractions.

Avoid duplicating logic and functionality across multiple files. Refactor repetitive code blocks into reusable components. Document reusable components clearly. Strive for simplicity; minimize complexity; Avoid over-engineering solutions. Prioritize readability, understandability, quality, maintainability, and testability. Only implement functionality that is currently required. Don't introduce features or code that is not explicitly needed. Focus on delivering working code, not anticipating future requirements.

Use consistent formatting/style, 2-space indentation, meaningful names, clear file names, judicious comments for complex logic, and docstrings for all functions, classes, and modules. Separate concerns into modules/components; use a module system. Include a README with clear instructions and an overview. Limit code to 180 lines; functions/classes ideally under 60 lines. Avoid unnecessary statements or blank lines. Refactor regularly; review and improve continuously; collaborate effectively.

Minimum: 80% code coverage. Test critical functionality: unit tests for components and integration tests for interactions.
